Apartheid. This system of institutionalized racial segregation in South Africa from nineteen forty-eight to the early nineteen nineties enshrined white minority rule through rigid racial classifications that determined where people lived, worked, and went to school. Nelson Mandela of the African National Congress spent twenty-seven years imprisoned resisting the system. International isolation through sanctions and cultural boycotts eventually delegitimized the regime, leading to majority-rule elections in nineteen ninety-four that installed Mandela as president.
